unit: words of the whole file, as `LC_ALL=C wc -w` counts them: a SKILL.md keyed by its skill's directory, frontmatter included, and a role file beside it keyed `<skill>/<file>`
raise: only in the commit that needs it, recorded in `raises` as {"from": <old>, "to": <new>, "why": "<the sentence skill-retro Step 4 asks for>"}; `skill-lint.py --against <ref>` fails a rise without one

skill-retro.why: Step 2 names the linter's new check, a `$` followed by a digit in a SKILL.md, which the Skill tool replaces with an argument when the skill loads: on 2026-10-21 harden's awk `$0` loaded as the first argument word, and a `{print $1}` in resolve-ticket's PRS lookup loaded as `{print --plan-only}`, so the five awk programs now use $NF, $(NF-1) and $(NF-NF)

pr-harden.why: Step 0 looks a PR's URL up in the local PRS file, a gh failure being a lookup to retry, to learn it resolves a private ticket the PR no longer names, and adopts one whose key only getJiraIssue reads; a new section, A private ticket's PR, has such a run re-check that before every brief, body edit and push, tell its reviewers and fixers so with the key (their role files carry what follows), count the key with grep -a in what each push publishes and rewrite unpushed commits that carry it, the one amend it allows, report what GitHub already shows, record pairings in a directory it chmods 700, send FINISH's list of what the loop did not implement and a blocking-only reviewer's notes to the report and the run record while still applying a finding that names the body, leave the PR a draft and keep its record local, with a pointer at each site that marks ready or writes to the PR description; and the State section's documented declined command now sits on one line, so pool-test's every-documented-invocation check runs it whole; the pre-push check counts from the merge-base of the PR head it fetches, so an unresolvable ref prints no count rather than 0 and a squash never reverts a moved base, rebuilds and re-verifies after a rewrite that changes a file, reads the title and body raw, and Step 0 records an adopted PR's pairing before any guard can refuse the run and refuses a private PR that is not a draft; the check fetches the PR head itself, since every fetch rewrites FETCH_HEAD, says to read its number rather than chain a push on grep's exit status, and refuses to squash over a merge, Step 0's already-public count joins its parts with && so a failure prints no number, the privacy bullet heads Step 0, and the fixer's brief carries the PR number; a rewrite runs in the same shell call as the check, a merge is made with a message naming no key, a tree-identical rewrite carries its verified sha over, and the already-public read includes comments and reviews; the count is a regex on the key's two halves so KEY_x and hyphenless test names count, the squash is one chained call with its merge test, a merge-blocked squash stops under the override pushing nothing, and the already-public read adds line comments, and before the PR exists the squash runs from the base's merge-base without the merge test, with its message file kept outside the worktree

pr-harden/fixer.md.why: the header says that on a private PR the brief gives the fixer the key, nothing it commits names it or the ticket's URL, in the message, a comment, a test name or a changeSet id, the message describes what the code now does in its own words, and it runs the pre-push check before reporting its sha, so the sha the verifier runs is the one pushed; it rewrites rather than only amends, building again if that changed a file; and the brief gives it the PR's number to fetch with, keeping any message file outside the worktree, and reporting a squash a merge stops instead of looping on it

pr-harden/reviewer.md.why: the header says that on a private PR the brief gives the ticket's key, and that the PR's silence about the ticket, and a body without the loop's declines, is deliberate and not a finding

resolve-ticket/refuter.md.why: the plan refuter's seven questions, the JSON it returns and the rule every objection must meet move here from SKILL.md byte for byte, beneath a new header that tells it to read the file first and what its brief carries, the shape pr-harden 0.36.0 gave the fixer and the verifier, once role-file-check's wave 1 passed (2026-09-28). The header and SKILL.md's pointer are new text, so resolve-ticket grows by both, for a refuter that reads its questions as written

resolve-ticket.why: Step 1 pre-flights the usage limit beside the verifier: a claude.ai usage limit ends the turn on an API error, which runs StopFailure rather than Stop, so no gate sees it and nothing in the skill runs again until a person, Claude Code or pool-run sends a turn, so a session started by hand checks CLAUDE_CODE_RETRY_WATCHDOG, under which a request at the limit, an agent's included, waits for the reset inside the turn (measured against a stub, artifacts/2026-10-21-retry-watchdog-limit), and when it is not on in any case of 1, true, yes or on says so at once and carries on, because Claude Code's own continue can be switched off for an account and skips Remote Control sessions, resets more than a day out and repeated hits, noting that a pool-run --work session may also have its launcher's nudge, and naming the remedy for later sessions, a shell alias with a five-hour usage-limit wait cap, read from Claude Code 2.1.301, and never a mid-run relaunch, which in a pool-run --work session releases the slot and leaves any relaunched session's gate entry owned by a dead pid

pr-review.why: Step 1 gains two sentences: a 404 from the JIRA endpoint can be a private ticket, so it is read with getJiraIssue, asking for the comment field it leaves out by default; and a ticket only that reads, or a PR the local PRS file lists, is private, so nothing posted on the PR names, quotes or links its ticket or says what the code let an attacker do; and where nothing settles a 404, as in CI, it says only that the tracker was unreachable

pr-review/posting.md.why: the first gate line says that on a private PR nothing posted names, quotes or links its ticket, whatever the third line's link rule asks, or says what the code let an attacker do, so a local run recites it before it posts or stages; the rule itself lives in SKILL.md, which the @claude review Action loads alone

ticket-pool.why: the sentence listing what a ticket argument may be says a private ticket's JIRA key is never one and not to queue one, because the pool cannot tell it from a missing key, its headless sessions cannot read it, and its driver writes a record named for the key into the store skill-retro publishes

ticket-pool/pausing.md.why: the paragraph on which sessions the --work carry reaches says what carries a session started by hand besides Claude Code's own wait, CLAUDE_CODE_RETRY_WATCHDOG, which resolve-ticket's Step 1 checks for, so the two skills no longer disagree about whether such a session can be carried past a usage limit
